attributes.title: An annotation tool for Japanese literary places

body.value:
Poetic places (called utamakura or meisho) have a long standing tradition in Japanese literature, creating a web of topographical references transcending genres of pre-modern writing. Mentioning a poetic place invokes earlier references and a set of textual or even pictorial connotations which gives a special depth to the text.
This program aims at mapping Japan’s most important literary places and providing detailed information on their historic, cultural, and poetic meaning.

This website is funded by the Ōsaka University.

In the past, the project has been funded by the National Institute of Japanese Literature NIJL-NW project within the NIHU Program for Young Researcher Overseas Visits for the year of 2017.

body.value:
Geographic location

Current maps (Google Maps) were used to identify the coordinates of the locations (sites, monuments, etc.). As for utamakura representing a wide area such as rivers and plains, characteristic landscapes (Mogami/Mogami river was located near the Shiraito waterfalls), famous historical sites, temples and shrines (Waka no ura was located near the Tamatsushima shrine) were used as criteria of definition. For more information on these characteristic landscapes, famous historical sites, temples and shrines Nihon rekishi chimei taikei (Heibonsha, 1979-2004) and Nihon kokugo daijiten dainiban (Shōgakukan, 2000-2002), Katagiri Yōichi's Utamakura utakotoba jiten (Kasama shoin, 1999), and Kubota Jun/Baba Akiko (ed.) Utakotoba utamakura daijiten (Kadokawa shoten, 1999) were used as reference.
In cases where it was difficult to link a name with any specific location as mentioned above, it was set near the center of a certain area or positioned at will near landmarks, post offices or government buildings.

 

Geographic information

Basic geographic information (administrative data, elevation, size of land, etc.) and other points worth mentioning such as the characteristics of the natural environment of the place, its location in relation to neighboring areas, the etymology of its name and how the area has been used throughout the history of Japan are described in detail. The information was provided mainly in reference to Nihon rekishi chimei taikei, Nihon kokugo daijiten dainiban, Kokushi daijiten (Yoshikawakō bunkan, 1979-1997) and Nihon daihyakka zensho (Shōgakukan, 1994).

 

History

The earliest reference to places and areas used as utamakura. Representative waka poems are included here that contributed to their construal as utamakura. If one area is closely associated with a poetic, literary work, a legend or narrative, or if there is a historical figure of special relevance for the area, an explanation has been added accordingly. It is noted when the name of a place refers to more than one location, or if it is impossible to locate it.
Main references used were Nihon rekishi chimei taikei, Kadokawa kokugo daijiten (Kadokawa shoten, 1982–1999) and Katagiri Yōichi's Utamakura utakotoba jiten. The cited examples have been confirmed in Shinpen Nihon koten bungaku zenshū (Shogakukan, 1994-2002) and Shin Nihon koten bungaku taikei (Iwanami shoten, 1989-2005).

 

Meanings as utamakura

Refers to what the utamakura specifically conjures up in the poems and texts. For example, in the case of "Otowa", it often appears in more concrete forms than "Otowa", such as "Otowa mountain", "Otowa river", "Otowa waterfall" and "Otowa village". Mainly Katagiri Yōichi's Utamakura utakotoba jiten was consulted for reference.

 

Characteristics as utamakura

The unique characteristics of the utamakura. Geographical information, famous landmarks, temples and shrines, or famous classics that are central when discussing the particular utamakura (e.g. in the case of "Akashi" The Tale of Genji) are given. If there is nothing of particular to note, it may be left blank. Mainly Katagiri Yōichi's Utamakura utakotoba jiten was consulted for reference.

 

Associations

Information not about the place itself, but about the images the utamakura evokes and connected terms like kakekotoba etc. are presented. In a first step, terms associated with any utamakura were identified using Haikai ruisenshū sakuin (Han'an Noma Kōshin-sensei kakō kinenkai, 1973–1975). In a second step, these were then narrowed down to around 10 words, using Katagiri Yōichi's Utamakura utakotoba jiten.

 

Images

The visual image of the specific area used as utamakura or the visual image of representative landscapes, temples and natural features in the area. These were mainly cited from illustrated guides (meisho zue) of the early modern period, such as Miyako meisho zue (An'ei 9 [1780]), Yamato meisho zue (Kansei 3 [1791]), Settsu meisho zue (Kansei 8 [1796] – Kansei 10 [1798]) etc., topographic works such as Rakuyō meisho shū (Manji 0 [1658]), Tōgoku meishōshi (Hōreki 12 [1762]) etc. and ukiyo-e prints such as the meisho-e of Utagawa Hiroshige and Katsushika Hokusai. This database complies with copyright agreements and CC licenses. Links that take you directly to the relevant pages are provided. As the National Diet Library's digital collection does not allow page by page linking, the National Institute of Japanese Literature's Shin Nihon kotenseki sōgō database was used mainly for books of classic literature. Databases of relevant museums (e.g. Tōkyō National Museum) were also included for paintings and picture scrolls (emaki).

September 15th 2020, written by Okabe Yuka & Kim Jihye

body.value:
・謡曲本文は、日本名著全集『謡曲三百五十番集』（日本名著全集刊行会、昭和3年）に拠った。

・題名は『謡曲三百五十番集』のものを基本とし、別名・別表記が存在する場合は（）内に示した。

・題名（ふりがな）は別名の場合には示したが、別表記で読みが同じ場合は略した。

・題名（ローマ字）は駅名標ヘボン式を採用した。複合名詞は「‐（ハイフン）」で区切り、2語目以降が固有名詞の場合、語頭を大文字にした。

・刊・完成・編纂（年）は近世・近代の明らかなもののみ加えた。中世以来の伝承曲は、諸説あるものもあるが、原則採らない。

・著者は作者を示した。主に『新版 能・狂言事典』（平凡社、2011年）の記述を用いたが、番外曲は主に田中允『未刊謡曲集』正続全53冊（古典文庫、1962年～1998年）を用いた。また適宜『能楽大辞典』（筑摩書房、2012年）・『日本国語大辞典』（小学館、2007年）等を参照した。

 

以下、非現行曲を中心に、各曲の詳細を記す。

・96《山姫》は非現行曲だが、明治末期から昭和初期まで喜多流の現行曲に含まれた曲。

・164《重盛》は非現行曲だが、明治末期から昭和初期まで喜多流の現行曲に含まれた曲。

・166《桜井》は『新版能・狂言事典』の《桜井駅》のこととした。『未刊謡曲集』続5には《桜井》《桜井駅》と題する同工異曲を6曲収載し、それぞれの関係性は複雑である。また165《楠露》とも同工異曲。

・167《正行》は非現行曲で、『未刊謡曲集』続13「金剛正本」の解題を参照した。ただし番外曲《花櫓》の改作で、同じく《正行》と題する同工異曲が存在するほか、喜多流の同名の番外曲《正行》（土岐善麿作）とは別曲である。

・184《菊慈童》は観世流のみの表記で、ほかの流派では《枕慈童》とする。185《枕慈童》は184《菊慈童》の改作で、同工異曲。

・191《笛の巻》は、観世流《橋弁慶》の前半の替え。

・c004《鼓滝》は、石井倫子「〈鼓滝〉と中世有馬」（『国文目白』49、日本女子大学国語国文学会、2010年2月）によった。

・c006《芳野》は『未刊謡曲集』続16の《吉野琴》解題によった。

・c011《吉野詣》は『未刊謡曲集』続6《明智討》改題によった。

・c023《宮城野》は同名異曲が複数あるが、この『謡曲三百五十番集』所収本は観世元章による明和改正本である。

・c030《島廻》は、『未刊謡曲集』続21の甲にあたる。同名異曲が存在する。

・c031《松浦物狂》は様々な系統がある。『未刊謡曲集』続21では甲・乙・丙・丁・戊・己の6種に分類しているが、この『謡曲三百五十番集』所収本は、甲にあたる。

・c033《松浦》は現在、観世流で《松浦佐用姫》の名で現行曲とされている曲。

・c034《粉川寺》は、『未刊謡曲集』続20の甲にあたる。同名異曲が存在する。

・c039《守屋》は、『申楽談儀』に井阿弥作の《守屋》の存在が記されるが、そこで引用された本文とは合致しない。

・c042《横山》は、その作者について諸説が存在し、決め手がないため、併記した。

・c043《春近》は、『未刊謡曲集』続19にて、異本が多く、本曲の本文批判は難事中の難であることが指摘される。「一応の分類」にて、この『謡曲三百五十番集』所収本は①にあたる。

・c044《十番切》は、観世流《夜討曽我》の小書「十番切」とは同名異曲。

・c049《現在千方》は、佐佐木信綱 校『新謡曲百番』（博文館、明治45年）の収録曲。田中允『評註謡曲全釈』（紫乃故郷舎、1950年）の記述により、近世期の作者不明曲として扱う。

・c050《泣不動》は、石井倫子「番外曲〈泣不動〉覚書」（『銕仙』427、銕仙会、1994年）によった。

（朝原広基作成）
